findings.section: Behaviour contract — C2 (the rule on words before the command name)
findings.summary: C2 refuses an expanded word that a wrapper skips, because it can become several words before the command name. The rule lists env, command, exec, nice, timeout, stdbuf and xargs, but not the option words of sh/bash/zsh/dash/ksh before the -c string. The judge handles those in shellString, not in the wrapper switch. Only the -c string holding $ is refused. An expanded option there can supply the command string, so this bypass gets through today and still gets through after B35.
findings.evidence: internal/fence/judge.go shellString skips any '-…' option without 'c' and the value of -o/+o, never looking for $. Base binary: `vloop fence check --phase review --tool bash 'IFS=,; sh -e$x -c ls'` → allow; `'sh -o $o -c ls'` → allow. Real shell, with a stub git on PATH: `bash -c 'x="c,git push"; IFS=,; sh -e$x -c ls'` printed `RAN push`, so it ran `git push`.
findings.fix: Extend C2's list: a word before the -c string of sh, bash, zsh, dash or ksh (an option, or -o's/+o's value) that expands refuses the command. Write the message literally. Today shellString's errors come out as `sh: <reason>`, so pick either `sh: -e$x expands before the command name and cannot be judged` or the unprefixed form. Add a worked-example line, e.g. `review  IFS=,; sh -e$x -c ls → deny: <that message>`, under # C2.

findings.summary: xargs appends words it reads from stdin after the command it runs. The judge looks through xargs and matches only the literal words, so `echo push origin | xargs git` is allowed today and after B35, and runs `git push origin`. This is the same class C2 closes: words the judge cannot see stand where a deny rule could match. The brief neither closes it nor names it in Out of scope. A previous round treated the arithmetic contexts this way.
findings.evidence: Base binary, work phase: `echo push origin | xargs git` → allow; `ls | xargs -I{} git {} origin` → allow. judge.go: `case "xargs": rest = skipXargs(rest)`, then the command is matched as written.
findings.fix: Either name it in Out of scope ("the words xargs appends from its input: matched as absent, as today; a later brief's"), or close it: treat an xargs command as followed by an expanded word, so `xargs git` is denied wherever `git push` is. Deferring is the smaller change.

findings.summary: C3 makes `command -v` run nothing, but only for `command`. In the code, `time` shares that wrapper case (`case "command", "time": rest = skipDashes(rest)`), so the obvious edit, putting the -v check in that case, also lets `time -v git push` through. GNU time -v does run the command. No worked-example line pins it.
findings.evidence: internal/fence/judge.go, words(): `case "command", "time":`. Base binary: `time -v git push` → deny: git push is denied by the review fence (Bash(git push:*)).
findings.fix: Add under # C3: `review  time -v git push → deny: git push is denied by the review fence (Bash(git push:*))`, and add "`time -v` let through" to the failures it must catch.

findings.summary: The domain entry cites S-2 but not S-4. S-4 is the invariant behind the new redirection rules on `}`, `done` and `)`: the worked example's `{ git status; } > .vloop/state/x` denial is S-4. The architect skill asks for every invariant that applies, by ID.
findings.fix: Make the entry "the glossary's **hook** row, S-2 and S-4: …, and the writes a redirection after `}`, `done` or `)` may make".

decisions: Read compounds by dropping the leading keyword, with no grammar parser (no mvdan.cc/sh). Agree: nothing inside is judged less than if it were written one command per line.
case, select, function, coproc and [[ stay refused. Agree; none appears among the counted denials.

An expanded word may be any text, the deliberate over-deny. The brief names `git diff "$BASE"`, `find "$d"` and `git diff -- src/*.go`. It does not name these two: in a work session `rm "$f"` and `rm *.tmp` are now denied (by `rm -r:*`), and `git log $BASE..HEAD` is denied everywhere (by `git log*--output*`). I'd keep the decision and add the rm case to the brief, so the operator sees the work-session cost.
Quoted means literal; `{}`, `@{u}` and `HEAD@{1}` are not brace expansions; `[` without `]` is not a glob. Agree.
C3 covers `command -v`/`-V` only, not type, which or hash (those are not looked through). Agree.
Subshells are read, but `((`, `$(`, `<(` and `>(` stay refused, and `((` is refused because of arithmetic. Agree.

A redirection target holding a glob is still judged as written. So `echo x > .gi?/hooks/pre-commit` is allowed in a work session, today and after B35. The driver's checks after the session, on .git/config, the hooks and .vloop/, and tee/cp being unjudged anyway, make this acceptable. It should be a conscious choice, though.
The let, ${a[x]} and declare -i arithmetic contexts stay out of scope. Agree.
Order within a command (opening keywords, then closing keywords/for/refused, then assignments and wrappers); a keyword after a wrapper is not dropped; C2 applies in every phase. Agree.
